findings.issue_text: registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate gate on getLoginPredicate(), which rejects non-BROKER_PUBLIC org-linked IDPs, but getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) caches those IDs; updating such an IDP (hideOnLogin, enabled, linkOnly) registers no invalidation, leaving stale cached login lists

getLoginPredicate() public SPI semantics changed (org-linked non-public IDPs no longer qualify) without mention, making other storage implementations/callers inconsistent with the JPA query for ALL/ORG_ONLY+orgId cases
getLoginPredicate() dereferences idp.getConfig() which can be null for a model with an organizationId, introducing a new NPE

Cache hit path in getForLogin returns models from getById without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, unlike the uncached/fallback paths, so callers get inconsistent org-aware semantics depending on cache warmth
remove() unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a DB round-trip) even when the IDP is in the cache and its model could be taken from the CachedIdentityProvider entry
When a cached ID resolves to null, only the current FetchMode's login key is invalidated, leaving the same stale ID in other modes' caches so each pays a separate DB fallback
OrganizationCacheTest cleanup uses literal string "alias" instead of the created alias, so the 21 created IDPs are never cleaned up and leak into subsequent tests
No test covers updating a non-public org-linked IDP's login attributes (hideOnLogin/enabled) after caches are populated; all org-linked IDPs in the test are BROKER_PUBLIC=true

Javadoc for registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate describes 'login IDP' per the predicate, which excludes non-public org IDPs that are actually returned by getForLogin(…, orgId), so the documented contract does not match cache contents

adjudication_records.issue_text: registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate gate on getLoginPredicate(), which rejects non-BROKER_PUBLIC org-linked IDPs, but getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) caches those IDs; updating such an IDP (hideOnLogin, enabled, linkOnly) registers no invalidation, leaving stale cached login lists

getLoginPredicate() public SPI semantics changed (org-linked non-public IDPs no longer qualify) without mention, making other storage implementations/callers inconsistent with the JPA query for ALL/ORG_ONLY+orgId cases
getLoginPredicate() dereferences idp.getConfig() which can be null for a model with an organizationId, introducing a new NPE

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(...))` to `getLoginPredicate()`. While this would NPE if `idp.getConfig()` were null and `organizationId` were non-null, the diff does not show (or change) any behavior that makes `getConfig()` nullable, nor does it provide evidence that `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` can be null. In Keycloak code, `getConfig().get(...)` is commonly used without null checks, implying the contract is that `getConfig()` is non-null. Therefore the finding depends on an unproven assumption and is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

remove() unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (a DB round-trip) even when the IDP is in the cache and its model could be taken from the CachedIdentityProvider entry

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff introduces `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check. That makes the delegate lookup happen on every remove() call, even when the IDP is present in the Infinispan cache (the `else` branch reads `CachedIdentityProvider cached = realmCache.getCache().get(...)`). Previously, the delegate lookup was only done in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path. So the finding that the change adds an unconditional delegate lookup even when cached data exists is directly verifiable from the diff (though whether it is strictly a DB round-trip depends on the delegate implementation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers updating a non-public org-linked IDP's login attributes (hideOnLogin/enabled) after caches are populated; all org-linked IDPs in the test are BROKER_PUBLIC=true

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching/invalidation for `getForLogin` and updates the login predicate to exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`. The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` indeed only links org IDPs that are public (i>=10) and does not exercise an org-linked, non-public IDP. However, that is a test-coverage observation, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: by definition such an IDP should not qualify for login, so updates to `hideOnLogin/enabled` would not be expected to affect the cached `getForLogin` results, and the invalidation code intentionally skips invalidation when both original and updated do not satisfy the login predicate. Nothing in the diff shows incorrect behavior stemming from this untested scenario.
